title: Per-route lifecycle orchestration for prompts & logs with consent tagging and deterministic evidence archives
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a per-route lifecycle orchestration system that lets teams declare TTLs and retention tags for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics. The system must support consent-aware overrides, deterministic evidence bundle exports for audits, and per-tenant residency constraints. Goal is to provide operators and compliance owners with an auditable, testable retention policy surface without requiring custom infra code per customer.
acceptance_criteria: UI/REST surface to define per-route retention policy (TTL, storage class, evidence window) exists and is documented
Policies can be scoped to route, model, and tenant; precedence rules are deterministic and documented
Consent tags can be attached to requests and will modify effective TTLs according to policy rules
Evidence export endpoint can produce a deterministic bundle for a given tenant + time range including prompts/responses/request logs/metrics with provenance metadata
Export respects data residency constraints and produces a verifiable manifest with SHA256 checksums and a signed timestamp
Automated test harness that validates TTL enforcement, export completeness, and residency routing is added to CI
Performance: retention enforcement background jobs do not increase p95 API latency and have configurable batching windows
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer deterministic, server-side bundle generation over ad-hoc per-tenant export scripts to simplify audits
Retention enforcement will be implemented as declarative rules evaluated at write-time and a compaction/eviction background worker for storage tiers
We will reuse existing KMS/HSM integrations for signing manifests; ensure key usage telemetry is recorded
Consider a 'consent:deleted' tag that triggers immediate pointer removal + archive into a short-lived quarantine bucket for legal hold processing
Must coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure on-prem export paths and residency are supported without cross-region leaks
Estimate assumes ENG will implement two core APIs (policy service + export job runner) and Console will add a minimal policy editor
